policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders a singular object, 'He showeth his word unto Jacob', against the plural 'his statutes and his ordinances' in the parallel line of the same verse. The qere base lemma dbrayw is plural ('his words'); the ketiv dbrw is the singular the ASV wording carries. The singular/plural contrast is visible in the English, so the ASV distinguishes the ketiv here.
